label: def:grothendieck-group-of-a-qou
title: The Grothendieck group of a quantum universe
html:
Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum universe over the commutative ring R.

Definition. The Grothendieck group K_0(\mathbf{C}) is the abelian group generated by the isomorphism classes [X] of objects of \mathbf{C}, subject to the relations [X \oplus Y] = [X] + [Y]. (This is the split Grothendieck group, the one appropriate to an additive category with no exact structure imposed; when \mathbf{C} is semisimple every short exact sequence splits and the two notions agree.)

The block presentation. Axiom 4 of a quantum universe, Wedderburn semisimplicity, provides a finite set \widehat{A} of blocks and a simple object V_\lambda for each block \lambda, such that every object is a finite direct sum of the V_\lambda (simple objects). Hence

  K_0(\mathbf{C}) \;=\; \bigoplus_{\lambda \in \widehat{A}} \mathbb{Z}\,[V_\lambda] \;\cong\; \mathbb{Z}^{\widehat{A}},

a free abelian group on the blocks. Two homomorphisms out of it are used in the paper. The rank K_0(\mathbf{C}) \to \mathbb{Z} sends [V_\lambda] to 1, so it counts simple constituents. The quantum dimension of a rigid monoidal category, \dim_q(X) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_X) \in \operatorname{End}(\mathbf{1}) = R, is additive under direct sums, so it extends to a homomorphism

  \dim_q \colon K_0(\mathbf{C}) \longrightarrow R, \qquad \sum_\lambda n_\lambda [V_\lambda] \longmapsto \sum_\lambda n_\lambda \dim_q(V_\lambda).

The ring structure. The tensor product of \mathbf{C} descends to K_0(\mathbf{C}), [X]\cdot[Y] = [X \otimes Y], because \otimes distributes over \oplus; with it K_0(\mathbf{C}) is a commutative ring when \mathbf{C} is braided, the fusion ring of \mathbf{C}, with unit [\mathbf{1}]. The quantum dimension is a ring homomorphism, since \dim_q(X \otimes Y) = \dim_q(X)\dim_q(Y) in a rigid braided category [kassel1995].

The example to keep in mind. For \mathbf{C} = \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), with simple objects V_n of dimension n + 1, the Clebsch–Gordan rule V_1 \otimes V_n = V_{n-1} \oplus V_{n+1} makes K_0(\mathbf{C}) = \mathbb{Z}[x] with x = [V_1]: each [V_n] is the polynomial in x determined by x\,[V_n] = [V_{n-1}] + [V_{n+1}], and the rank of [V_n] is 1 while \dim_q [V_n] = [n+1]_q. The quantum group \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) at generic q has the same simple objects, the same Clebsch–Gordan rule, and hence the same Grothendieck ring; what changes with q is not the group K_0 but the homomorphism \dim_q out of it. That is the sense in which the quantum dimension, and not the Grothendieck class, is the q-dependent object [bghl-2017].
